description: A serene private home office with a clean, minimalist Japandi-influenced aesthetic. The room centers on a large oval-edged desk with a white stone or marble top and warm light-oak base, flanked in front by two low rounded armchairs in white shell forms with sage-green upholstered cushions and walnut-stained legs. A matching sage-green executive chair sits behind the desk. A small circular side table in light oak occupies the foreground between the visitor chairs. The desk surface holds a laptop, a glass vase with delicate branching stems, a small pencil cup, and a playful decorative figure. Behind the desk, the feature wall is clad in floor-to-ceiling vertical fluted plaster paneling in crisp white, providing soft architectural texture without ornamentation. To the right, floor-length natural linen curtains pool gently at the edge of a tall window, diffusing daylight into warm cream tones. A potted olive-style tree in a white ceramic pot stands tall beside the curtains. To the left, a floor-to-ceiling glass partition wall hints at an adjacent corridor. The flooring is wide-plank pale blonde oak in a straight-lay pattern. A warm glow runs along the ceiling perimeter from a recessed cove strip, and a long brass rod suspended overhead casts even diffused warm illumination downward across the desk surface.
